posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
> **favalora:** Nice!I will be at SPIE-IS&T Electronic Imaging for the 3D display conference (which is always oddly decoupled from Practical Holography, at a different site). Perhaps I'll at least get the proceedings of the holography one...

For what it's worth, there was some discussion a few years back about the connection between Holography and 3D. There was a vote on whether the holographers should go with SPIE or with IS&T. I believe that if the holographers voted to stay with SPIE which meant that we could no longer go to the 3D conference because they were holding their meeting at a different site at a different time. I remember at the time having a longish discussion with Joel Kollin and Pierre St. Hilaire. Joel (as I remember) said that if there was a split, he'd migrate to the IS&T 3D conference. As is well known, the holographers did split off from the 3D, which, for me anyway, meant that I don't see some of the usual faces I used to see in San Jose. Of course, all of this is dragged from memory so I may be hazy on some of it.

posts.author: favalora
posts.content_md:
Yes, these symposia (collections of conferences) are REALLY expensive. Generally, you can attend any of the conferences that are on the same site as the one you registered for. For example, if you register for Electronic Imaging, you can wander around the various conferences that are all part of Electronic Imaging. The Practical Holography conference is part of Photonics West, or something, right? I would bet that the SPIE website will tell you what conferences you can attend. (Or you can call them, they're helpful and friendly.)

g
